measurement: does batching candidates into one Lean invocation pay?
premise: results/rung2_gate_cost.json showed the whole cost is a fixed Mathlib.Tactic.Ring load per invocation (bare floor median 17.61 s, the slowest of four conditions). Batching pays that once for many candidates. This tests that prediction instead of asserting it.
atomicity: A batch containing one false obligation fails as a whole and yields no per-candidate verdict, so it must be re-run individually to isolate. That is the measured cost of the lever, not a caveat.
how_to_read_it: The same-input spread on this host reaches 2.60x, so a saving below that is unmeasurable (LL.md 29.12). Compare the speedup against the spreads reported per condition, not against zero.
not_established: N=8, R=3. Small samples; medians with spreads, not distributions.
A persistent Lean server was not built; this measures batching into one file, which is the cheap approximation of process reuse.
The break-even failure rate assumes isolation re-runs every candidate; a bisection would be cheaper and is not measured.

decomposition.reading: A candidate's own elaboration costs about 0.14 s; roughly 97% of a single verification is fixed per-invocation overhead. That is why batching pays and why caching a verdict, modularising a genome or importing the spec instead of inlining it cannot: none of them touches the fixed term.

a_magnitude_correction_to_LL_29_13: LL.md 29.13 quoted the fixed per-invocation cost as a median 17.61 s, from results/rung2_gate_cost.json. Here a single candidate verifies in a median 5.37 s. The earlier figures were taken BEFORE `lake build ANSE.VerletSymplectic` had produced an olean, so the spec was re-elaborated from source and the toolchain caches were colder. The STRUCTURE of that conclusion is unchanged and is in fact sharper here -- the fixed term dominates at ~97% and the candidate's own work is negligible -- but the absolute magnitude is cache-state dependent and the 17.61 s figure should not be quoted as the cost of a verification on a warm host.
verdict: The lever is REAL and large: 7.16x over 8 candidates, with a batch spread of 1.02x, so it is resolvable far above the host noise that made every proposal-round claim unmeasurable. Batching loses only above a failure rate of 84.2%, which no realistic search reaches. It remains a process-architecture change with no evolutionary or biological content.
